name: Illinois
summary: Statutes, Constitution and Admin Code: the official ilga.gov host refuses both routes from this workspace (WebFetch ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, shell TLS failure), so text comes only from tier 2 — Justia (ILCS 2025, whose long article/chapter pages truncate near 120K chars; Constitution) and Cornell LII (Admin Code). Court rules, Rules of Evidence, opinions (Supreme Court from 1996, Appellate Court, Rule 23 orders) and PLA disposition lists are on illinoiscourts.gov, which links through a 302 to blob-storage PDFs: fetch_doc.py follows it and reads them in full (the only route to Supreme Court Rules index rows past ~Rule 573, incl. the Rules of Professional Conduct); WebFetch needs two calls. Opinion search is ASP.NET POST-only; RSS feeds give recent opinions by GET. Illinois has public-domain citations (2021 IL 125656; 2026 IL App (1st) 232256-U) from July 1, 2011, and the Appellate number maps to the docket (1-23-2256).

citation_map.notes: Ill. S. Ct. R. 6 (verified): cases filed on or after July 1, 2011 are cited by public-domain citation — 'YYYY IL NNNNNN' (Supreme Court) or 'YYYY IL App (Nth) NNNNNN' (district: 1st, 2d, 3d, 4th, 5th) — with paragraph pinpoints ', ¶ 15' / ', ¶¶ 21-23'; Rule 23 orders add '-U'; earlier published cases are cited to the Official Reports (Ill., Ill. 2d, Ill. App., Ill. App. 2d/3d), N.E. and Ill. Dec. optional. Docket mapping (observed on Wancket/Moore and PLA lists): the six-digit Appellate number is the docket — 2026 IL App (1st) 232256 = No. 1-23-2256; the Supreme number is the Supreme docket (2021 IL 125656 = No. 125656). Workers' Compensation Division cites carry 'WC' (e.g. '141234WC'; from memory). Suffixes -B/-C (modified/upon rehearing) from memory. Rule 23 orders: not precedential; per Rule 23(e)(1) as amended (eff. Jan. 1, 2021, from memory) orders entered on or after that date may be cited for persuasive purposes. Routing guards: bare 'Rule 23', 'Supreme Court Rule 41' or 'Section 2-619' do not route here without 'Ill.'/'Illinois' or an Illinois act name (the Supreme Court Rule regex requires 'Ill. S. Ct. R.', 'Illinois Supreme Court Rule' or '… of the Illinois Supreme Court Rules'). N.E. and WL cites route here only with an '(Ill.' parenthetical (N.E. also covers IN, MA, NY, OH). 'Ill. Reg.' and 'Ill. Adm. Code' are distinct from reporter cites because a digit must follow 'Ill.' for the reporter regex. Ranges: '735 ILCS 5/2-619 to 2-622' captures only the first section; the section group refuses a trailing hyphen-digit run. Pre-1993 citations to Ill. Rev. Stat. ('Ill. Rev. Stat. 1991, ch. 110, par. 2-619') have no free source here; ch. 110 = 735 ILCS 5. CourtListener ids from memory: 'ill' (Supreme Court of Illinois), 'illappct' (Appellate Court of Illinois) — unverified. Generic act names (Wrongful Death Act, Survival Act, Open Meetings Act, Eviction Act, Limited Liability Company Act, Freedom of Information Act) exist in other states: the prose-form ILCS alternative routes here only when the query has Illinois context; otherwise ask or treat as ambiguous. Appellate dockets may carry a letter suffix (1-26-0690B) or 'WC'; the docket regex accepts both. Survival Act and Eviction Act aliases point to the Article/section where they sit (755 ILCS 5/27-6; 735 ILCS 5/Art. IX).

sources.official_status_evidence: Final opinions carry the 'Illinois Official Reports' header (Rehfield, 2021 IL 125656); since July 1, 2011 the public-domain citation is the citation form required by Ill. access.pattern_rules: The opinion URL uses a guid that is not derivable from the citation; the file name on the blob host after the 302 is '{Case name} {citation}.pdf' (e.g. 'Rehfield v. Diocese of Joliet, 2021 IL 125656.pdf') but the guid is still needed. Finding an opinion: (1) the listing page shows the latest ~150 rows (case name link, citation, filing date, court, Opinion/Rule 23, status); (2) the search form is ASP.NET POST-only (GET query strings such as ?ctl00$ctl04$txtFilterName=… are ignored — tested): fields ctl00$ctl04$txtFilterName (free text — matches opinion full text, not just party names: searching 'Rehfield' also returned cases citing it), ddlFilterFilingDate ('Search All Years'), ddlFilterCourtType ('Supreme Court', 'First District Appellate Court' … 'Workers' Compensation'), ddlFilterType ('Opinion' | 'Rule 23'), ddlFilterStatus; hdnSortField=FilingDate, hdnSortDirection=ASC|DESC; results 150 rows per page, paged by __doPostBack Page$N. (3) RSS (plain GET, XML): /views/courts/rss/opinions-supreme.aspx and /views/courts/rss/opinions-appellate.aspx with opinion:citationnum, filingdate, court, docketstatus and a link of the form https://www.illinoiscourts.gov/resources/{guid}/{Case name} {citation}.pdf containing raw spaces — percent-encode spaces as %20 before fetching; it also 302s to the blob host.
access.navigation: SCRIPT FIRST: listing / POST search / RSS -> fetch_doc.py read/grep /resources/{guid}/file (or the RSS .pdf link, spaces %20-encoded); the script follows the 302 to the blob PDF. Fetch tool: /resources/{guid}/file -> reported Location -> blob PDF.
access.read_via: Script: fetch_doc.py follows the 302 from www.illinoiscourts.gov/resources/{guid}/file to ilcourtsaudio.blob.core.windows.net and reads the full PDF (blob host's 401/403 robots reply = no rules, RFC 9309). Fetch tool: two hops.

script_candidates.why: RSS feeds by plain GET (/views/courts/rss/opinions-supreme.aspx, opinions-appellate.aspx) carry citationnum, filing date, court, status and the PDF link; the ASP.NET POST search (full-text filter, court, type, status, sort) returns structured rows with guid links — a script can resolve a public-domain citation to its PDF. fetch_doc.py reads the blob PDFs.
Index is one GridView table (Article, Rule N, guid link, 'Amended … eff. …') readable by fetch_doc.py: a script can map 'Ill. S. Ct. R. N' -> guid and amendment date deterministically.
Dated PLA lists keyed by appellate docket; the citation->docket mapping is deterministic, so a script could index all lists 2007-2026 by appellate docket (fetch_doc.py reads the blob PDFs).

corpus_candidates.why: Index page (145,695 chars) exceeds the fetch tool's ~105K window (Articles VI-XI rows unreachable by WebFetch); text is ~400 separate per-rule PDFs behind a redirect. fetch_doc.py reads both the index and the PDFs, so a corpus is ingestible.
